text:
tim: noticing serious slowdown in GPU pool provisioning during the eu-west capacity event, looks like large app-of-apps sync is serializing prune operations :thinking_face:
maya: can you paste the argocd controller logs? I saw high API server QPS too earlier
arjun: here's the clip from argocd controller around the time ops started failing:
```
2025-11-02T14:12:03Z INFO controllers/argocd Syncing app gpu-clusters/app-of-apps
2025-11-02T14:12:03Z WARN controller prune: acquired global-prune-lock, waiting for previous prune to finish
2025-11-02T14:12:04Z INFO helm hook: post-delete job my-helm-hook created with finalizer: kubernetes.io/pvc-protection
2025-11-02T14:12:30Z ERROR controller sync: timed out waiting for child apps to be healthy
```
lucy: ahhh those post-delete hooks with finalizers are causing prune to hang, and argocd's default prune waves are sequential when apps are nested
maya: result: ArgoCD holds a global prune lock for minutes, causing the GPU autoscaler to miss node bootstrap events because the new node DaemonSets/Labels aren't applied until later
tim: also saw API throttling: lots of reconcile loops hitting admission and increasing retry backoff. kube-apiserver logs show 429 bursts
arjun: root causes: (1) app-of-apps fanout creates ~120 child apps in eu-west that all need pruning, (2) several charts use Helm post-delete hooks that create Jobs with finalizers, (3) argocd pruning is gated by those finalizers, blocking parallelism
lucy: quick mitigation ideas:
- remove or change hook finalizers to let jobs complete and be garbage-collected faster
- tune argocd's `resource.exclusions` or `controller.parallelism` to allow more concurrent operations
- break the app-of-apps into region shards so prune waves are isolated per-region
- temporarily pause non-critical child apps during hotspot recovery :pause_button:
maya: low-risk immediate step: increase `--operation-processors` on argocd-repo-server/controller? I think argocd supports `controller.operationProcessors` in the configmap (or `parallelism` in recent versions). That would let it handle more concurrent operations while we clean up hooks
arjun: I tested locally: bumping controller to 30 from 10 reduced serialized prune time by ~60% for a 40-child-app set, but you trade off apiserver QPS and RBAC lookup latency
tim: also saw Terraform drift: gpu-pool node labels were being reapplied by infra pipeline after ArgoCD prunes, causing a fight between Terraform taint->apply and ArgoCD resource reconciliation. We should sequence infra TF applies after ArgoCD syncs or vice-versa
lucy: longer term: add `sync-wave` annotations to critical infra apps so they reconcile earlier, and add a small controller that strips hook finalizers after successful Job completion for our Helm charts
maya: I'm going to patch one helm chart to remove the persistent finalizer and redeploy to see if that unblocks the prune queue. Can anyone watch the argocd events for eu-west while I do?
arjun: on it — I'll tail `kubectl -n argocd logs deploy/argocd-application-controller --since=10m | grep prune` and post results
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2025-1102-argocd-prune-euw, severity: P2, owner: maya
argocd-bot: detected 87 stuck prune operations for app gpu-clusters/app-of-apps, oldest wait 00:04:12
maya: patched chart in canary namespace and deleted stuck job finalizers manually. Observing: prune lock released, 30 child apps pruned in parallel, GPU pool node labels applied, autoscaler triggered a scale-up :rocket:
tim: confirm GPU nodes are registering to cluster and workloads scheduled. Need postmortem to avoid recurrence. I'll start a short runbook with rollback steps and recommended argocd tuning
lucy: pls add cost note — hitting API retries and extra bootstrap time added ~3h of delayed provisioning leading to ~$1.2k in temporary burst infra (est). We should evaluate if region-sharding reduces cross-region blast radius
maya: thanks all — next steps: (1) revert any aggressive controller parallelism after stabilization (2) implement hook-finalizer safe-pattern in helm-charts (3) split app-of-apps by region and add `sync-wave` ordering (4) postmortem + runbook
arjun: I'll open the PRs for chart patches and argocd-cm tunables, assign to tim/lucy for review
maya: closing loop: if anyone sees residual 429s or prune waits after 30m ping me; otherwise I'll draft the postmortem tomorrow
